matches.label: load
rules: A canceled load was a load, and counts as booked. It does not count as delivered.
A load belongs to the customer: the parent account of the site that shipped it.
A load is booked on the date of its first tender: the row where orig_load_id is empty. Booking dates use the UTC date of crt_ts.
A row in the load table is a tender, not a load. A re-tendered load has two rows and is still one load.
A test load or a voided load is not a load.
rules_checked_against_data: A load is booked on its first tender: the row that does not point to an earlier row. A re-tender is not a second load.
A load is one shipment, counted once: it has exactly one first tender.
A test load or a voided load is not a load.
Revenue and loads belong to the parent of the site that shipped.

matches.label: billable load
rules: A load can be invoiced only when a signed proof of delivery is on file. An unsigned document does not count.
Test loads are never billed. They are not waiting on anything.
The invoice is cut the day the signed proof of delivery is received. A delivered load without one has no invoice and no revenue yet.
warehouse_source: bil_pod_doc: a row for the load with signed_flg true

matches.label: canceled load
rules: Canceled-load fees billed to the customer are revenue, in the period of the fee date. The carrier's share of a canceled-load fee is a cost in the period of the fee date.
The rated linehaul on a canceled row of the load table was never billed.

matches.label: delivered load
rules: A delivered load belongs to the calendar day, month and quarter of its arrival at the final delivery stop, on the clock at that stop.
A load with two delivery stops is delivered once, at the last one.
Delivered is not the same as billable. Billing waits for a signed proof of delivery.
Only real loads count: not test rows, not voided rows. A re-tendered load is delivered once, by the carrier on its final row.
rules_checked_against_data: A load is delivered when the carrier on its final row reports the final delivery: status DLVD. A canceled load does not count as delivered.
warehouse_source: tms_load_hdr.load_stat_cd = 'DLVD'; arrival at the last delivery stop in tms_stop (arr_ts, tz_nm).

matches.label: tender
rules: When the first carrier accepts a load and then falls off, the load is tendered again and a second row is written. The second row points to the first through orig_load_id. The first row keeps status RTND and is never deleted. Both rows carry the same linehaul revenue.
rules_checked_against_data: The account on a load is a shipping site, and the account that pays is a bill-to party. Neither is the customer.
warehouse_source: tms_load_hdr: one row per tender. load_id identifies the row; orig_load_id is filled on a re-tender.

matches.label: revenue
rules: Revenue belongs to the customer: the parent of the site that shipped.

Revenue is the invoice total, which already includes linehaul, fuel surcharge and accessorial charges billed to the customer, less credit memos in the period of the credit date, plus canceled-load fees billed to the customer in the period of the fee date, all in US dollars.
The rated linehaul on a tender (tms_load_hdr.lh_rev_amt) is not revenue: it leaves out fuel and accessorials, and it sits on canceled, test, voided and re-tendered rows that were never billed.
